articles.title: IFS Capital Signs S$79 Million MSME Loan Securitization With CapitaLand Investment
articles.snippet:
IFS Capital has signed its inaugural S$79 million loan securitization program backed by a portfolio of micro, small and midsize enterprise loans secured by Singapore real estate.
The post IFS Capital Signs S$79 Million MSME Loan Securitization With CapitaLand Investment appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
IFS Capital Signs S$79 Million MSME Loan Securitization With CapitaLand Investment
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 2, 2026
IFS Capital Signs S$79 Million MSME Loan Securitization With CapitaLand Investment
IFS Capital has signed its inaugural S$79 million loan securitization program backed by a portfolio of micro, small and midsize enterprise loans secured by Singapore real estate. DBS Bank is serving as sole arranger for the transaction.
IFS Capital will sell a defined pool of loans from its existing MSME portfolio to a special purpose vehicle, which will finance the purchase by issuing senior, mezzanine and subordinated notes.
CapitaLand Investment will subscribe for the full aggregate principal amount of the senior notes issued on the first issue date.
IFS Capital will retain the mezzanine and subordinated notes, aligning its interests with the senior note investor over the life of the pool.
The notes will have a four-year tenor, and IFS Capital will continue servicing the underlying loans. Existing borrower relationships will not change.
The securitization will allow IFS Capital to recycle capital currently committed to loans through maturity and redeploy those funds into additional MSME lending.
The company plans to develop securitization into a recurring funding and capital management channel across multiple product portfolios.
IFS Capital’s private credit business provides working capital, asset-based and property-secured financing to MSMEs across Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Hong Kong.
Group lending assets totaled S$475 million as of June 30, 2026.
KEY QUOTES:
“A transaction like this rests on an investor’s confidence in how we underwrite and how our loans perform over time. We are pleased to have CapitaLand Investment as an investor in our first securitisation. We have structured the transaction in a way that aligns our interests with those of our investor for the life of the pool. Our intention is to make this a repeatable channel, with capital continuously being put back to work for MSMEs in the region.”
Randy Sim, Group Chief Executive Officer of IFS Capital
“This investment expands CapitaLand Investment’s exposure to Singapore’s real estate private credit market and advances our fund management growth strategy in the credit sector. We are pleased to partner with IFS, whose capabilities and market expertise complement CapitaLand Investment’s regional credit investment platform. The senior secured notes provide stable, risk-adjusted returns backed by a diversified portfolio of real estate assets. We continue to see compelling opportunities in real estate private credit across developed Asia Pacific markets.”
Arjun Pandit, Managing Director and Head of Credit, Private Funds at CapitaLand Investment
“This transaction demonstrates how securitisation can unlock institutional capital, enhance funding diversity and support the flow of capital to the real economy. DBS is pleased to have brought together IFS Capital and CapitaLand Investment in this inaugural transaction. Beyond its significance for the parties involved, it marks an important step forward in the continued development of Singapore’s securitisation market.”
Clifford Lee, Managing Director and Global Head of Investment Banking at DBS Bank

articles.title: Tiger Finance Deploys $78 Million In Q3 Asset-Based Financing
articles.snippet:
Tiger Finance committed $78 million in new asset-based financing to retail and consumer products companies during the third quarter of 2026, deploying capital across refinancing transactions, growth initiatives, dividend recapitalizations, and supplemental liquidity facilities.
The post Tiger Finance Deploys $78 Million In Q3 Asset-Based Financing appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Tiger Finance Deploys $78 Million In Q3 Asset-Based Financing
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 20, 2026
Tiger Finance Deploys $78 Million In Q3 Asset-Based Financing
Tiger Finance committed $78 million in new asset-based financing to retail and consumer products companies during the third quarter of 2026, deploying capital across refinancing transactions, growth initiatives, dividend recapitalizations, and supplemental liquidity facilities.
The lending platform, which operates as a division of Tiger Capital Group, structured the quarterly commitments through revolving credit facilities, term loans, and first-in, last-out debt. The financings supported both private equity-backed and non-sponsored borrowers.
The largest transaction during the quarter was a $33 million FILO term loan for women’s fashion retailer Maurices. Tiger Finance acted as agent on the facility and participated alongside Wingspire Capital as part of a broader refinancing of Maurices’ balance sheet.
The refinancing extended debt maturities and reduced borrowing costs for Maurices, which operates more than 800 stores. The transaction also expanded an existing lending relationship between Tiger and Maurices that began in 2023.
Tiger Finance also provided a $20 million revolving line of credit to Garage Beer, a premium light beer brand backed by Jason and Travis Kelce and Durational Capital Management. The facility is intended to support new product development and expansion into additional markets.
The Garage Beer transaction represents Tiger Finance’s second financing for a portfolio company backed by Durational Capital Management.
The third major commitment was a $25 million term loan to a large U.S. department store chain. The borrower used part of the proceeds to repay maturing higher-cost debt and increase liquidity, including liquidity used to support dividend payments to equity holders.
Tiger Finance focuses on secured lending structures that use assets including working capital, machinery and equipment, fixtures, real estate, and intellectual property as collateral. Its financing solutions for middle-market businesses include first-lien, second-lien, and split-lien facilities, frequently structured as term debt.
The platform draws on Tiger Capital Group’s broader asset valuation capabilities. Tiger said the organization appraises and sells more than $30 billion of inventory, brands, and other consumer assets annually, providing data that informs its underwriting and financing structures.
KEY QUOTE:
“Borrowers across the retail and consumer sectors are seeking flexible financing that both reflects the value of their assets and provides them the capital to execute on their business plans. Tiger appraises and sells in excess of $30 billion annually of inventory, brands, and other consumer assets every day. That lets us lend against them with confidence and structure facilities that go beyond a conventional borrowing base.”
Bob DeAngelis, Executive Managing Director And Group Head Of Tiger Finance

articles.snippet:
Endeavor Catalyst has expanded its Middle East portfolio to 64 companies across six markets, with $76.6 million invested in the region, up 22 times from $3.5 million a decade ago. The regional growth follows the final close of Endeavor Catalyst Fund V, an oversubscribed $320 million fund that increased the firm's total assets under management to more than $850 million.
The post Endeavor Catalyst Expands Middle East Portfolio To 64 Companies With $76.6 Million Invested appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Endeavor Catalyst Expands Middle East Portfolio To 64 Companies With $76.6 Million Invested
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 21, 2026
Endeavor Catalyst Expands Middle East Portfolio To 64 Companies With $76.6 Million Invested
Endeavor Catalyst has expanded its Middle East portfolio to 64 companies across six markets, with $76.6 million invested in the region, up 22 times from $3.5 million a decade ago. The regional growth follows the final close of Endeavor Catalyst Fund V, an oversubscribed $320 million fund that increased the firm’s total assets under management to more than $850 million.
The investment platform now backs companies across Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. Regional portfolio companies include Tabby, MNT-Halan, Tamara, Kitopi, and Moove. Endeavor Catalyst said the Middle East has also become an increasingly important source of realizations within its global portfolio.
Three of the 15 liquidity events across Endeavor Catalyst’s portfolio since the start of 2025 have come from the Middle East, making the region second only to Latin America for recent realizations. The Middle East portfolio has produced five exits in total.
Endeavor Catalyst operates as a co-investment fund, investing alongside venture capital and growth equity firms in companies led by founders who have been selected into the Endeavor network. Fund V will continue backing founders in markets where the firm sees ambition and company creation growing faster than access to capital.
The firm’s Dubai Global Hub is part of that strategy, connecting founders in the region with investors, mentors, and operators across markets. More than 90 Endeavor Entrepreneurs from 20 countries are based in the Dubai hub. Globally, Endeavor’s network includes more than 3,100 entrepreneurs across more than 50 countries, while Endeavor Catalyst has backed 437 companies across 44 Catalyst markets. Its portfolio includes 83 companies valued at $1 billion or more and 39 exits.
KEY QUOTES:
“The past few years have been tumultuous in the Middle East. Some outside the region might think that’s a reason not to invest, but at Endeavor Catalyst we know the opposite is true. The response to the disruption has shown just how ambitious and determined Middle Eastern founders are. With Fund V, we’re continuing our bet that big challenges lead to big impact.”
Yana El Dirani, Regional Lead For Endeavor Catalyst And Managing Director For Endeavor’s Dubai Global Hub

articles.title: Tishman Speyer Secures $75 Million Second Close For Korea Living Venture, Bringing Commitments To $395 Million
articles.snippet:
Tishman Speyer has secured a $75 million commitment from a German pension fund in the second closing of its Korea Living Venture, bringing total equity commitments to the residential investment vehicle to $395 million.
The post Tishman Speyer Secures $75 Million Second Close For Korea Living Venture, Bringing Commitments To $395 Million appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Tishman Speyer Secures $75 Million Second Close For Korea Living Venture, Bringing Commitments To $395 Million
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 5, 2026
Tishman Speyer Secures $75 Million Second Close For Korea Living Venture, Bringing Commitments To $395 Million
Tishman Speyer has secured a $75 million commitment from a German pension fund in the second closing of its Korea Living Venture, bringing total equity commitments to the residential investment vehicle to $395 million.
The new investment builds on KLV’s first closing, which secured $300 million in commitments from APG Asset Management and Bouwinvest.
Combined with Tishman Speyer’s $20 million of sponsor equity, the capital effectively achieves the firm’s initial $400 million fundraising target.
Tishman Speyer expects the equity commitments to support more than $800 million of total investment capacity when anticipated financing is included.
The Korea Living Venture is focused on building a diversified portfolio of residential properties across the Seoul Metropolitan Area, where Tishman Speyer sees increasing demand for rental housing.
The fund primarily targets existing residential properties offering opportunities for value enhancement while maintaining selective exposure to development projects.
Its investment strategy focuses on properties near major transportation hubs with convenient access to business districts and university campuses in Seoul, Icheon, Gyeonggi-do and other high-growth neighborhoods throughout the capital region.
Tishman Speyer said Seoul’s rental market is benefiting from structural demographic and economic changes, including rising housing costs, an increasing number of single-person households and growing populations of foreign residents and international students.
KLV completed its first acquisition in August 2026 with the purchase of Songdo CoStay, a stabilized 411-unit residential property in Songdo, Incheon, South Korea.
The nine-story property is located in the Songdo International Business District, an area that includes multiple universities and approximately 70 biotechnology and life sciences companies.
Songdo CoStay consists of furnished residential units supported by a range of shared amenities.
The acquisition gives KLV an initial operating asset while the venture continues seeking additional investments throughout the Seoul metropolitan region.
KLV also expands Tishman Speyer’s broader global diversification strategy as the real estate investment firm increases its exposure to residential properties and other asset classes across additional markets.
Since 2023, Tishman Speyer has acquired approximately 3,800 residential units across 13 communities in three countries and 10 U.S. states.
Over the same period, the firm has commenced or completed construction of approximately 4,100 rental apartments.
Tishman Speyer currently has approximately 7,400 residential units in its development pipeline.
Across its broader global real estate platform, Tishman Speyer has acquired, developed and operated 600 properties totaling approximately 242 million square feet since its founding in 1978, representing a combined value of approximately $138 billion.
KEY QUOTE:
“This second closing of our KLV fund reflects continued investor conviction in Korea’s living sector. These partnerships position us well as we continue to scale a high-quality, diversified residential portfolio across the Seoul Metropolitan Area.”
Graham Mackie, Head of Pan-Asia at Tishman Speyer

articles.title: Vertical Semiconductor Signs Letter Of Intent For Up To $73 Million In CHIPS Act Funding To Advance AI Data Center Power Technology
articles.snippet:
Vertical Semiconductor, a Boston-based power semiconductor company spun out of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, has signed a letter of intent with the U.S. Department of Commerce for up to $73 million in proposed funding under the CHIPS and Science Act.
The post Vertical Semiconductor Signs Letter Of Intent For Up To $73 Million In CHIPS Act Funding To Advance AI Data Center Power Technology appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Vertical Semiconductor Signs Letter Of Intent For Up To $73 Million In CHIPS Act Funding To Advance AI Data Center Power Technology
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 22, 2026
Vertical Semiconductor Signs Letter Of Intent For Up To $73 Million In CHIPS Act Funding To Advance AI Data Center Power Technology
Vertical Semiconductor, a Boston-based power semiconductor company spun out of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, has signed a letter of intent with the U.S. Department of Commerce for up to $73 million in proposed funding under the CHIPS and Science Act.
The funding would support research, development, and commercialization of next-generation vertical gallium nitride power transistors intended to improve electricity delivery for artificial intelligence data centers and other high-performance computing infrastructure.
The proposed financial assistance would be provided through the Department of Commerce’s CHIPS Research and Development Office and is designed to accelerate domestic development and production of advanced power semiconductor technologies.
Vertical Semiconductor is developing a vertical gallium nitride FinFET platform intended to deliver greater power efficiency and higher power density than conventional semiconductor power conversion approaches.
Gallium nitride is a semiconductor material used in high-performance power electronics because of its ability to support efficient electrical switching and operation under demanding conditions.
The company’s vertical transistor architecture is designed to reduce energy losses during power conversion while limiting heat generation and the physical space required for electrical infrastructure.
These capabilities are becoming increasingly important as AI data centers require substantially more electricity to power advanced processors and other computing systems.
Vertical Semiconductor believes that improvements in power conversion efficiency could allow data center operators to deploy additional computing capacity without requiring proportional increases in available grid power.
The company’s technology originated from research supported by the U.S. Department of Energy’s Advanced Research Projects Agency–Energy.
The proposed CHIPS funding would support further development of the technology and help establish domestic production capabilities for vertical gallium nitride devices.
As part of the initiative, Vertical Semiconductor plans to collaborate with commercial partners on a demonstration involving a 2.5-megawatt AI computing rack.
The proposed system is designed to demonstrate how vertical gallium nitride technology can improve power delivery throughout the data center infrastructure.
According to the company, the demonstration aims to reduce energy losses by approximately 30% while decreasing the physical footprint of power conversion equipment by 50%.
These improvements could allow a greater portion of available electricity to reach computing equipment rather than being lost during conversion and distribution.
The project also intends to demonstrate the benefits of deploying advanced semiconductor devices throughout the AI data center power chain, from grid connections to computing hardware.
Vertical Semiconductor sees the technology as an opportunity to help address one of the primary infrastructure constraints affecting the expansion of AI computing capacity.
